domain_label: Study System — KG Architect: Learning Science of Knowledge Graphs
purpose: The learning-science slice of the knowledge-graph architect: how the theory of concept maps (Novak & Cañas 2008) and Knowledge Space Theory (Doignon & Falmagne 1985) dictate what a Concept node and a typed ConceptEdge should mean, which graph shapes actually aid learning and retrieval, how a prerequisite DAG and its learning fringe drive 'block new cards on a concept until its prerequisite is mastered', and when to graduate a flat prerequisite spine into a full cross-linked graph — kept honest by tagging every domain claim FACT/ESTIMATE-to-source-verify/UNKNOWN and tracing every app-behavior claim to APP_RECON.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all base scores are heuristic priors and every shape/threshold recommendation is an ESTIMATE synthesized from the cited learning-science literature, not a measured result on this deck

the app's Concept and ConceptEdge entities are the fixed integration target: ConceptEdge carries a typed relation in {prereq, related, part_of} with src/dst concept ids and Concept is a per-exam named unit [FACT-source: APP_RECON entity schemas]

the prerequisite-gating behaviour this KB reasons about ('block new cards until prereq mastery >= 0.6') exists as diagnosis-string text only and is enforced by no code today [FACT-source: APP_RECON §4a] — this KB specifies the learning-science logic a real gate would implement, not a claim that it is implemented

the two other kgraph KBs (knowledge-representation/ontology-engineering and biomedical terminology entity-linking) own the schema-mechanics and term-normalization slices; this KB stays in the learning-science slice and only names those boundaries
exclusions: the ontology-engineering mechanics (formal typed node/edge schema design, hub-node graph algorithms, RDF/property-graph choices) that a neighboring kgraph KB owns, beyond mapping learning-science relations onto the existing ConceptEdge enum
medical/dental terminology recognition, synonym normalization and hover-definition attachment (the neighboring biomedical-entity-linking kgraph KB), beyond naming a Concept node's granularity
the visual encoding, layout and color-palette rendering of the graph (the viz specialist), beyond specifying WHAT the color-coded meaning layer must express
the per-concept mastery estimator itself (BKT/Elo, owned by the learner specialist), consumed here only as the mastery signal a prerequisite gate reads
authoring or LLM-generating the actual edge instances for the INBDE/TOEFL decks (contenteng), beyond the graduation policy for when the flat spine becomes a full graph

competency_questions.question: Why represent a study domain as a graph at all, and what is the 'meaning layer' this KB owns versus the raw edge table contenteng produces?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that a graph makes prerequisite and integrative structure explicit so sequencing and gating become computable, and separates the data layer (edge rows) from the learning-science meaning layer (what a node/edge should signify)

competency_questions.question: What are the defining features of a Novak & Cañas concept map, and which of them does the app's ConceptEdge keep or drop?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names concepts-as-nodes, labeled linking phrases forming propositions, a focus question, hierarchical layout and cross-links, and notes ConceptEdge keeps typed direction but drops the free-text linking phrase

competency_questions.question: What is a knowledge structure in Knowledge Space Theory and what is a knowledge state?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: defines a knowledge structure as a family of knowledge states (subsets of domain items a learner can have mastered) containing the empty and full sets, with the Doignon & Falmagne 1985 citation

competency_questions.question: What extra axioms turn a knowledge space into a learning space, and what are the outer and inner fringes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states learning-smoothness/accessibility and closure-under-union (well-gradedness) let every state be reached one item at a time, and defines the outer fringe as the items learnable next and the inner fringe as the most recently learnable

competency_questions.question: How does the surmise relation formalize 'prerequisite', and why must prerequisite edges form a DAG?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: explains that mastering an item lets one surmise mastery of its prerequisites (a quasi-order underlying a quasi-ordinal knowledge space), so prerequisite edges must be acyclic or they assert a contradiction, and a topological order is a valid learning sequence

competency_questions.question: Which graph shapes actually aid learning and retrieval, and which harm them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that a sparse hierarchy with a few meaningful cross-links aids organization and retrieval while an over-dense hairball degrades both, tying this to organized/elaborated structure and spreading activation, all tagged ESTIMATE-to-source-verify

competency_questions.question: What are hub/anchor concepts, what do they do for learning, and what is their risk?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: defines hub nodes as high-degree integrative anchors (subsumption/cross-link concentrators) that organize a domain but risk becoming over-connected bottlenecks that gate too much

competency_questions.question: How do prerequisite edges and the learning fringe drive 'block new cards on a concept until its prerequisite is mastered'?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: describes gating a dependent concept's new cards until every prerequisite's mastery clears a threshold (the app's block-until->=0.6 rule off bkt_p_mastery), grounded in the outer fringe as the set of currently unlockable concepts, traced to APP_RECON

competency_questions.question: What goes wrong with prerequisite gating and how is it bounded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names over-gating (frustration, deadlock from a mislabeled or cyclic DAG, orphaned concepts) versus under-gating, and prescribes an escape hatch, a hysteresis band and a DAG-acyclicity precheck

competency_questions.question: When should the graph graduate from a flat prerequisite spine to a full cross-linked graph?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: prescribes starting with a hierarchical tree/prerequisite spine and adding related/cross-link edges only as co-mastery or authoring evidence accrues, so early sparsity avoids a premature hairball

competency_questions.question: How do the three ConceptEdge types map onto learning-science relations, and what should a Concept node's granularity be?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: maps prereq->surmise/DAG, part_of->hierarchical composition, related->associative cross-link, and sets a Concept node to a single masterable/testable unit (a KST item) rather than a whole chapter

competency_questions.question: What does KST add beyond the edge table contenteng deferred, and what is the recommended graph-model verdict for this app?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states KST supplies knowledge states, the learning fringe and the surmise-based gate contenteng punted (KG_RECON §2a), and gives the verdict: hierarchical concept-map backbone + prerequisite DAG for gating + sparse cross-links, graduating flat-spine->graph, mapped onto Concept/ConceptEdge and feeding the color meaning layer

glossary.definition: A graphical knowledge representation in which concepts are nodes and each edge carries a labeled linking phrase so that concept-link-concept reads as a proposition; maps are organized hierarchically around a focus question with cross-links joining separate branches [FACT — cited in contenteng KBs per SPECIALIST_LIST §C1].

A concept-link-concept triple whose edge label makes it a readable statement (e.g. 'caries -> is caused by -> acidogenic bacteria'); the unit of meaning in a concept map and the feature the app's unlabeled typed ConceptEdge drops.

Doignon & Falmagne (1985) set-theoretic framework modelling a domain as a family of knowledge states — the subsets of items a learner could plausibly have mastered together — rather than a single ability score [FACT — cited in contenteng KBs per SPECIALIST_LIST §C1].

A subset of domain items a learner has mastered; the family of all admissible states is the knowledge structure, which always contains the empty set (knows nothing) and the full domain (knows everything).

A knowledge structure satisfying learning-smoothness/accessibility (any nonempty state can be reached by adding one item at a time) and closure under union (well-gradedness); its states form the reachable learning paths [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

The precedence relation in which mastering item b lets one surmise mastery of its prerequisites a; for a quasi-ordinal knowledge space this quasi-order (Birkhoff correspondence) IS the prerequisite structure and must be acyclic [ESTIMATE — to source-verify].

For a knowledge state, the outer fringe is the set of items the learner could learn next (the study frontier) and the inner fringe is the most recently learnable items; the outer fringe is exactly the set of currently unlockable concepts a gate exposes.

A high-degree node that integrates many others — an Ausubelian subsumption anchor or a cross-link concentrator; it organizes a domain but risks becoming an over-connected bottleneck that gates too many downstream concepts [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the subsumption framing].

The directed acyclic graph of ConceptEdge type='prereq' edges; acyclicity is required because a cycle asserts that a concept is its own prerequisite, and a topological ordering of the DAG is a valid study sequence.

Withholding a dependent concept's new cards until every prerequisite concept's mastery clears a threshold; the app's diagnosis text is 'block new cards on this concept until prereq mastery >= 0.6', triggered when a prereq's bkt_p_mastery < 0.5, and is text-only with no enforcing code today [FACT-source: APP_RECON §4a].

The staged buildout in which the graph begins as a hierarchical tree or a single prerequisite spine and gains related/cross-link edges only as co-mastery or authoring evidence justifies them, keeping early graphs sparse and legible.

nodes.definition: Frame the learning-science reason to represent a study domain as a graph rather than a flat card list: a graph makes prerequisite precedence and integrative structure EXPLICIT and therefore computable — you can topologically sequence study, gate on prerequisites, and locate integrative anchors. This KB owns the MEANING layer (what a node and a typed edge should signify for learning) as opposed to the DATA layer (the raw ConceptEdge rows contenteng emits) and the RENDER layer (colors/layout, owned by viz). contenteng stops at an edge table and explicitly defers the full Knowledge Space Theory treatment [FACT-source: SPECIALIST_LIST §C1, KG_RECON §2a]; this KB supplies the learning science that gives those edges their instructional meaning [ESTIMATE — design synthesis over the cited theory].

included: the learning rationale for a graph representation
the boundary against contenteng's deferred KST
excluded: the formal edge schema mechanics (neighboring KB)
the color/layout rendering (viz)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change to the contenteng edge table or the viz boundary revises the frame

pros.claim: Separating the meaning layer from the raw edge table stops the graph from being a decorative overlay and makes sequencing and gating first-class
pros.example: reading a prereq edge as a study-order constraint rather than just a drawn line between two Concept rows

cons.claim: The meaning layer is a synthesis over learning-science literature, not a measured result on this deck, so its recommendations are judgments data could revise
cons.example: asserting a sparse hierarchy helps before any retention data on this app confirms it

failure_modes: treating the graph as visual decoration with no instructional consequence
conflating the meaning layer with the render layer and duplicating viz's job
acceptance_tests: the frame states the graph's sequencing/gating rationale, the data-vs-meaning-vs-render split, and the contenteng-defers-KST boundary with the source tag
revisit_triggers: contenteng changes what the edge table contains
the viz specialist redefines the render-layer boundary
retention data contradicts a meaning-layer recommendation

nodes.definition: Enumerate the defining features of a Novak & Cañas (2008) concept map: concepts (perceived regularities, usually noun-labeled) are the NODES; every link carries a LABELED linking phrase; a concept-link-concept triple is a PROPOSITION (the unit of meaning); the map is built around a FOCUS QUESTION; it is arranged HIERARCHICALLY with the most general concepts at the top; and CROSS-LINKS join otherwise-separate branches to show integration [FACT — cited in contenteng KBs per SPECIALIST_LIST §C1]. Concept mapping rests on Ausubelian assimilation theory: meaningful learning attaches new concepts to relevant existing ones, which is exactly what an anchor/hub node models [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the Ausubel attribution]. This is the qualitative, human-readable pole of knowledge-graph theory.

included: concepts-as-nodes, labeled links, propositions, focus question, hierarchy, cross-links
excluded: the formal set-theoretic KST view (its own node)
the ConceptEdge mapping (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a schema change adding linking phrases or a source-verification of the Ausubel link updates the feature set

pros.claim: The concept-map feature set gives a concrete, evidence-backed template for what a good node and a good edge look like to a learner
pros.example: requiring each authored edge to read as a proposition rather than an unlabeled arrow

cons.claim: Full concept maps demand a free-text linking phrase per edge that the app's typed ConceptEdge cannot store, so fidelity is partial
cons.example: collapsing 'is treated by' and 'is contraindicated in' both into a single 'related' type and losing the proposition

failure_modes: dropping the focus question and letting the map sprawl without a purpose
authoring unlabeled links so no proposition is expressed
acceptance_tests: the six concept-map features are listed with the Novak & Cañas citation and the assimilation-theory grounding is tagged ESTIMATE-to-source-verify
revisit_triggers: the ConceptEdge schema gains a linking-phrase field
the focus-question framing changes for a deck
the assimilation-theory attribution is source-verified or corrected

nodes.definition: Make the proposition the unit of meaning and reconcile it with the app's typed edges. In a concept map the edge label carries the semantics: 'periodontitis -> is characterized by -> attachment loss' is a proposition a learner can be tested on, and elaborative interrogation (asking WHY the link holds) is a known retrieval booster [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. The app's ConceptEdge stores only a TYPE in {prereq, related, part_of} and a direction, not a free-text phrase [FACT-source: APP_RECON entity schema], so the propositional content is compressed into the type plus the two concept names. The design consequence: choose the three types so that the recovered proposition ('A is a prerequisite of B', 'A is part of B', 'A is related to B') is still instructionally meaningful, and keep richer linking phrases in card text where they can be authored freely.

included: the proposition as unit of meaning
elaborative interrogation as a retrieval lever
how the typed ConceptEdge compresses a proposition
excluded: the full edge-type-to-relation mapping (its own node)
term-level linking in card text (biomedical KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a linking-phrase field or a catch-all 'related' problem changes the propositional mapping

pros.claim: Treating each edge as a compressed proposition keeps the typed graph instructionally meaningful despite the missing linking phrase
pros.example: reading a prereq edge as the testable claim 'you must know A before B makes sense'

cons.claim: Three fixed types cannot express the diversity of real linking phrases, so nuance lives only in card text and is invisible to the graph
cons.example: 'inhibits' and 'is a cofactor of' both flattening to 'related' at the graph level

failure_modes: overloading 'related' as a catch-all so it carries no meaning
expecting the graph type alone to convey a nuance that only card text holds
acceptance_tests: the node states the proposition-as-meaning principle, notes ConceptEdge stores only a type (source-tagged), and prescribes choosing types whose recovered proposition stays meaningful
revisit_triggers: a linking-phrase field is added to ConceptEdge
the 'related' type is observed to be an unusable catch-all
elaborative-interrogation evidence is source-verified

nodes.definition: Distinguish the two structural axes of a concept map: HIERARCHY (general concepts subsume specific ones top-to-bottom, the tree backbone) and CROSS-LINKS (edges joining separate branches, signalling integrative, often creative, understanding) [FACT — Novak & Cañas feature, cited per SPECIALIST_LIST §C1]. The hierarchy maps naturally onto part_of / prereq edges and gives the graph its spine; cross-links map onto 'related' edges and are the sparse connective tissue that turns a set of trees into a graph. Good maps have MANY hierarchical edges and FEW, high-value cross-links — cross-links are prized precisely because they are rare and integrative, which is the structural argument against a dense hairball [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the cross-link-quality claim].

excluded: hub-node degree analysis (its own node)
the density thresholds for retrieval (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a density target or an observed over/under-connection changes the hierarchy/cross-link balance

pros.claim: Naming the two axes tells the author which edges are structural spine (many) and which are integrative cross-links (few and precious)
pros.example: building the INBDE tree first, then adding a handful of cross-links between pharmacology and pathology

cons.claim: The 'few cross-links' guidance is qualitative, so without a density target authors can either over-connect or omit the integrative links that make the map valuable
cons.example: adding a cross-link between every co-occurring pair and recreating a hairball

failure_modes: adding cross-links indiscriminately until the hierarchy is unreadable
omitting cross-links entirely and leaving disconnected trees
acceptance_tests: the node separates hierarchy from cross-links, maps each onto edge types, and states the many-hierarchical/few-cross-link balance with the quality claim tagged ESTIMATE
revisit_triggers: a density target is set by the graph-shapes node
cross-links are observed to over- or under-connect a deck
the integrative-value claim is source-verified

nodes.definition: State the formal, quantitative pole: Knowledge Space Theory (Doignon & Falmagne 1985) models a domain as a KNOWLEDGE STRUCTURE — a family of KNOWLEDGE STATES, where a state is the subset of domain items a learner could plausibly have mastered together — instead of a single scalar ability [FACT — cited in contenteng KBs per SPECIALIST_LIST §C1]. The structure always includes the empty set (knows nothing) and the full domain (knows everything). Not every subset is a valid state: which subsets are admissible is governed by the domain's prerequisite structure, so KST turns 'what does the learner know' into 'which state are they in', and the graph edges are what constrain the set of admissible states. This is the theory that gives a Concept node the identity of a masterable ITEM.

included: knowledge structure as a family of states
a state as a subset of mastered items
excluded: the learning-space axioms (its own node)
the surmise/prerequisite relation formalism (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: domain growth or a weak prerequisite structure changes the state-space treatment

pros.claim: Modelling knowledge as a state rather than a score captures that two learners with the same count can know different things and need different next items
pros.example: distinguishing a learner who mastered anatomy-then-pharmacology from one who did the reverse at the same total

cons.claim: The full family of states is exponential in the number of items, so KST is only tractable when the prerequisite structure sharply restricts admissible states
cons.example: a 500-concept domain having astronomically many subsets unless prereq edges prune them

failure_modes: treating every subset as an admissible state and losing tractability
collapsing a knowledge state back into a single mastery score
acceptance_tests: the node defines a knowledge structure and state, names the empty/full states, and ties admissibility to the prerequisite structure with the Doignon & Falmagne citation
revisit_triggers: the domain grows large enough that state enumeration matters
the prerequisite structure is found too weak to prune states
the item granularity changes what counts as a state element

nodes.definition: Add the two axioms that make a knowledge structure a LEARNING SPACE: (1) learning smoothness / accessibility — any nonempty admissible state can be reached from the empty state by adding one item at a time, each intermediate set also being a state; and (2) closure under union — the union of any two states is a state (well-gradedness) [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. Together these guarantee that from any state there is always a single-item step forward, so the learner is never stuck and there is always a legitimate 'next thing to learn'. This is the theoretical justification for one-concept-at-a-time sequencing and for a study frontier that never dead-ends, and it is what a prerequisite DAG must preserve to be a valid learning space.

excluded: the outer/inner fringe definitions (its own node)
the DAG acyclicity requirement (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an axiom violation in an authored graph or a source-verification changes the learning-space treatment

pros.claim: The learning-space axioms guarantee a stepwise, never-stuck study path, which is exactly the property a sequencer needs
pros.example: always being able to hand the learner one unlockable concept regardless of their current state

cons.claim: Real authored prerequisite graphs may violate the axioms (a state with no single-item exit), producing dead-ends the theory forbids
cons.example: a concept whose two prerequisites can only be satisfied simultaneously, breaking accessibility

failure_modes: authoring a prerequisite graph that admits a dead-end state with no single-item step
assuming well-gradedness holds without checking the authored edges
acceptance_tests: the node states both axioms, derives the always-a-next-step guarantee, and tags the axiom statements ESTIMATE-to-source-verify
revisit_triggers: an authored graph is found to violate accessibility
a dead-end state is observed in practice
the axioms are source-verified against Falmagne & Doignon

nodes.definition: Formalize 'prerequisite' as the SURMISE relation: if observing mastery of item b lets you surmise (infer) mastery of item a, then a precedes b. For a quasi-ordinal knowledge space the admissible states are exactly the down-sets of a quasi-order on items, and by the Birkhoff correspondence that quasi-order IS the prerequisite structure — so the prerequisite graph and the knowledge space are two views of one object [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the Birkhoff/quasi-ordinal statement]. This is the bridge from concept-map hierarchy and KST states to the app's ConceptEdge type='prereq': a prereq edge asserts a surmise dependency, and the set of all such edges defines which knowledge states are reachable. It also means a prerequisite relation must be transitive-consistent and, crucially, acyclic.

included: the surmise relation as prerequisite precedence
the quasi-order / down-set correspondence to states
excluded: the DAG acyclicity mechanics and topological order (its own node)
the gating behaviour (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a need for soft prerequisites or a source-verification of the quasi-ordinal link changes the prerequisite formalism

pros.claim: Grounding prereq edges in the surmise relation gives the app's prereq type a precise, testable meaning tied to the state space
pros.example: justifying a prereq edge only when mastering the successor genuinely implies mastering the predecessor

cons.claim: Real prerequisites are often soft or probabilistic, not the hard surmise the quasi-ordinal model assumes, so strict edges can overstate necessity
cons.example: marking a helpful-but-not-required concept as a hard prerequisite and needlessly blocking study

failure_modes: asserting a prereq edge where the dependency is merely helpful, not surmisable
ignoring transitivity so redundant prereq edges pile up
acceptance_tests: the node defines the surmise relation, links it to the quasi-order/down-set view of states (tagged ESTIMATE), and maps it onto ConceptEdge type='prereq'
revisit_triggers: soft/probabilistic prerequisites are needed
transitive-redundant edges accumulate
the quasi-ordinal claim is source-verified

nodes.definition: Define the fringes of a knowledge state, the operational output of KST for sequencing: the OUTER FRINGE is the set of items the learner could learn NEXT — each is one item whose addition yields another admissible state — and the INNER FRINGE is the set of items most recently learnable (removing one still leaves a state) [ESTIMATE — to source-verify]. The outer fringe is precisely the set of currently UNLOCKABLE concepts: every prerequisite of an outer-fringe item is already mastered. This is the concrete bridge to gating — 'what should I study now' is answered by the outer fringe, and 'is this concept unlocked yet' is answered by whether it sits on the outer fringe of the learner's current state. The inner fringe flags what to review to consolidate a state.

included: outer fringe as the next-learnable/unlockable set
the fringe as the sequencing output
excluded: the mastery-threshold mechanics of the gate (its own node)
the gating risk analysis (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fringe instability from estimate noise or a re-ranking need changes the frontier logic

pros.claim: The outer fringe turns the abstract state space into a directly usable 'study these next' list a UI can render
pros.example: surfacing exactly the concepts whose prerequisites are all mastered as the unlocked set

cons.claim: Computing the true fringe requires knowing the learner's exact state, which is only estimated (noisy BKT mastery), so the fringe is an estimate not a certainty
cons.example: a concept flickering on and off the outer fringe as a borderline prerequisite mastery estimate wobbles

failure_modes: computing the fringe from a point mastery estimate without accounting for its noise
confusing the inner fringe (review) with the outer fringe (learn next)
acceptance_tests: the node defines outer and inner fringe, identifies the outer fringe as the unlockable set feeding the gate, and tags the definitions ESTIMATE-to-source-verify
revisit_triggers: mastery-estimate noise makes the fringe unstable
the UI needs a different next-item ranking
the fringe definitions are source-verified

nodes.definition: Require the prerequisite edges to form a DIRECTED ACYCLIC GRAPH. A cycle in prereq edges asserts that a concept is (transitively) its own prerequisite — a contradiction that makes some concepts permanently unlockable and breaks the learning-space accessibility guarantee. So before the graph is used for gating it must pass an acyclicity check, and any TOPOLOGICAL ordering of the DAG is then a valid end-to-end study sequence [FACT — standard graph property; its application here is design synthesis]. The app's diagnosis walks prereq edges to find an unmastered prerequisite [FACT-source: APP_RECON §4a], which only terminates safely if the edges are acyclic; a cycle would let a naive walk loop. This node is the correctness gate on the whole prerequisite layer.

included: topological order as a valid study sequence
excluded: the gating mechanism that consumes the DAG (its own node)
the surmise semantics of each edge (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a detected cycle or a looping prerequisite walk changes the acyclicity handling

pros.claim: An enforced acyclic prerequisite DAG guarantees a valid global study order and a terminating prerequisite walk
pros.example: topologically sorting concepts so every concept appears after all its prerequisites

cons.claim: Authoring or LLM-generation can easily introduce a cycle, and without an explicit check the gate silently deadlocks or loops
cons.example: an LLM adding A->B and B->A prereq edges that lock both concepts forever

failure_modes: shipping a prereq graph with an undetected cycle that permanently blocks concepts
walking prereq edges without a visited-set and looping on a cycle
acceptance_tests: the node requires an acyclicity precheck, states topological order as a valid study sequence, and ties a cycle to permanent unlockability and walk non-termination
revisit_triggers: a cycle is detected in an authored or generated graph
the prerequisite walk is observed to loop or stall
the acyclicity check is added or changed

nodes.definition: State which graph SHAPES actually aid learning and retrieval and which harm them: a SPARSE, mostly HIERARCHICAL graph with a small number of high-value cross-links supports organized encoding and legible study paths, whereas an OVER-DENSE 'hairball' (near-complete connectivity) degrades both — it offers no sequencing signal, overwhelms the learner, and makes any gate block almost everything [ESTIMATE — to source-verify; grounded in concept-map hierarchy evidence and network-organization arguments]. Moderate, meaningful connectivity is the target: enough edges to express real prerequisites and integrative links, few enough that the structure remains a readable tree-plus-cross-links rather than a mesh. Concretely, favour low average out-degree on prereq edges and reserve 'related' edges for genuinely integrative pairs.

excluded: retrieval-mechanism specifics (its own node)
hub-node degree analysis (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured density threshold or an observed hairball trend changes the shape target

pros.claim: A shape target lets an author or generator be told concretely to keep the graph sparse and hierarchical rather than maximally connected
pros.example: capping related-edge density so the graph stays a tree-plus-cross-links

cons.claim: The 'sparse is better' guidance is an ESTIMATE without a deck-specific density threshold, so the exact cutoff is a tunable judgment
cons.example: not knowing whether 1 or 3 cross-links per branch is the right budget for INBDE

failure_modes: letting connectivity grow into a hairball with no sequencing signal
over-pruning until the graph is disconnected trees with no integration
acceptance_tests: the node names the sparse-hierarchy target and the hairball anti-pattern, gives the out-degree/related-reservation heuristics, and tags the shape claims ESTIMATE-to-source-verify
revisit_triggers: a deck-specific density threshold is measured
the graph is observed to trend toward a hairball
disconnection harms integration

nodes.definition: Characterize HUB / ANCHOR concepts: high-degree nodes that many others depend on or link to. In assimilation terms a hub is a subsumption anchor — a general concept new material attaches to — so hubs are where integrative understanding concentrates and are natural entry points for a domain [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the subsumption framing]. But a hub carries a specific graph-shape RISK: because a prerequisite hub sits upstream of many concepts, if it is mislabeled or set as a hard prerequisite it gates a large downstream subgraph, and an over-connected hub can make the graph brittle. The design rule: allow a few deliberate hubs as organizing anchors, watch their out-degree on prereq edges, and never let an accidental hub silently become a global bottleneck.

included: the downstream-gating and brittleness risk of prerequisite hubs
excluded: the general density target (its own node)
hub graph-algorithm computation (neighboring ontology KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an accidental-hub bottleneck or an over-prune of anchors changes the hub policy

pros.claim: Recognizing hubs lets the design use a few of them as intentional anchors while guarding against accidental bottlenecks
pros.example: designating 'cell metabolism' a deliberate anchor while flagging an accidental 20-child prereq hub for review

cons.claim: The line between a useful anchor and a harmful bottleneck is a judgment, and over-caution can strip the graph of the anchors that aid organization
cons.example: removing a legitimate foundational hub because its degree looked high

failure_modes: an accidental prerequisite hub gating a huge downstream subgraph
stripping legitimate anchors in the name of sparsity
acceptance_tests: the node defines hubs as high-degree anchors, states the downstream-gating/brittleness risk of prerequisite hubs, and gives the deliberate-few-hubs rule with degree-watching
revisit_triggers: an accidental hub is found gating a large subgraph
an anchor is over-pruned
a hub-degree threshold is set

nodes.definition: Explain WHY the right structure aids retrieval, not just encoding. Organized, hierarchically structured material is recalled better than a flat list, and elaborated links (knowing WHY A connects to B) give more retrieval routes — the concept-map linking phrase and the 'related' cross-link are the graph's carriers of that elaboration [ESTIMATE — to source-verify; spreading-activation and organized-recall arguments]. Spreading activation predicts that retrieving one concept partially primes its graph neighbours, so a moderately connected graph creates helpful retrieval cues while a hairball creates interference. The design consequence for this app: the graph is not only a sequencing device but a retrieval scaffold, so edges should encode real, elaborable relationships, and this is a further argument for meaningful-but-sparse connectivity over maximal connectivity.

included: organized-structure and elaboration as retrieval boosters
spreading activation as the neighbour-priming mechanism

nodes.definition: Give the graduation policy from a FLAT prerequisite SPINE to a FULL cross-linked graph. Early, with little data and few concepts, model the domain as a hierarchical TREE or a single linear prerequisite spine — this is legible, trivially acyclic, and enough to sequence study. Add 'related' cross-link edges and additional prereq branches only as EVIDENCE accrues: co-mastery patterns (concepts learned together), authoring signals (a card explicitly bridges two concepts), or observed confusions [ESTIMATE — design synthesis over the graph-shape and concept-map evidence]. The rule is deliberate sparsity first, connectivity earned later, so the graph never starts as a hairball and each added edge has a justification. This is the structural counterpart of the learner-model 'start simple, add complexity only when data supports it' discipline.

nodes.definition: Specify how prerequisite edges and the learning fringe drive 'BLOCK new cards on a concept until its prerequisite is mastered'. The mechanism: a dependent concept is UNLOCKED (its new cards may be introduced) only when every concept upstream of it via prereq edges has mastery clearing a threshold — equivalently, only when the concept lies on the learner's OUTER FRINGE. The app already encodes this as a diagnosis rule: when a missed concept has any prereq concept with bkt_p_mastery < 0.5 it emits 'missing_prereq' and the fix string 'Schedule the prerequisite concept first; block new cards on this concept until prereq mastery >= 0.6' — but this blocking is TEXT ONLY, enforced by no code today [FACT-source: APP_RECON §4a]. This node supplies the learning-science logic a real enforcing gate would implement: walk prereq edges, check each prerequisite's mastery, and withhold new cards until all clear.

included: the app's existing text-only missing_prereq rule as the integration target
excluded: the specific threshold and hysteresis values (its own node)

nodes.definition: Set the mastery threshold logic for the gate. The app uses an asymmetric band: a prerequisite counts as WEAK (triggering the missing_prereq diagnosis) when its bkt_p_mastery < 0.5, but the unblock condition is stated as mastery >= 0.6 [FACT-source: APP_RECON §4a]. Read as a HYSTERESIS band, this gap (0.5 to unlock-fail, 0.6 to unlock-pass) is exactly the guard against a concept flickering unlocked/locked as a borderline mastery estimate wobbles across a single threshold [ESTIMATE — the hysteresis interpretation is design synthesis; the two numbers are FACT]. The design rule: gate on a band, not a point; require the prerequisite to reach the higher bound to unlock and only re-lock if it falls below the lower bound; and choose the band wide enough to absorb mastery-estimate noise but narrow enough not to over-block.

included: the hysteresis interpretation against threshold flicker
excluded: how mastery itself is estimated (learner KB)
the broader gating risks (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: persistent flicker or a re-tune of the 0.5/0.6 values changes the threshold band

pros.claim: A hysteresis band stops a concept oscillating between locked and unlocked as a borderline mastery estimate jitters

cons.claim: The specific 0.5/0.6 values are the app's choice, not a validated optimum, so the band width is a heuristic that may over- or under-block
cons.example: a 0.6 bar being too high for a concept the learner could handle at 0.55

failure_modes: gating on a single point threshold and flickering on noise

nodes.definition: Bound the failure space of prerequisite gating. OVER-GATING harms: a mislabeled or too-strict prereq edge, or a cyclic DAG, can DEADLOCK a concept (permanently unlockable), orphan concepts behind an unreachable prerequisite, or frustrate a learner who is actually ready. UNDER-GATING harms: too few or too-weak prerequisites let a learner drill advanced material with no foundation, wasting effort. The mitigations: run the acyclicity precheck (from the DAG node) before gating; provide an explicit ESCAPE HATCH so a learner or author can override a block; keep the hysteresis band so borderline mastery does not thrash; and cap prerequisite chain depth so no concept sits behind an unreasonably long unlock path [ESTIMATE — design synthesis]. A gate with no override is more dangerous than no gate, because a single bad edge silently removes content.

included: escape hatch, acyclicity precheck, hysteresis, chain-depth cap mitigations
excluded: the acyclicity mechanics themselves (DAG node)
the threshold values (threshold node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a deadlock report or override misuse changes the gating-risk mitigations

pros.claim: Naming both failure directions and the escape hatch keeps a single bad prereq edge from silently starving the learner of content
pros.example: letting a learner override a block on a concept a wrong edge locked

cons.claim: An escape hatch that is too easy to hit dissolves the gate's value, so the override must be deliberate not default
cons.example: a one-tap skip that learners use to bypass every legitimate prerequisite

failure_modes: shipping a gate with no override so a bad edge permanently hides content
making the override so easy the gate never actually gates
acceptance_tests: the node names over-gating and under-gating harms and prescribes the escape hatch, acyclicity precheck, hysteresis, and chain-depth cap as mitigations
revisit_triggers: a deadlock or orphaned concept is reported
the override is over- or under-used
a prerequisite chain is found too deep

nodes.definition: Map the three ConceptEdge types onto learning-science relations so authors and generators use them consistently. PREREQ = the surmise/precedence relation forming the acyclic study-order DAG (must be mastered before). PART_OF = hierarchical/mereological composition (this concept is a component of that broader one) — the concept-map hierarchy backbone, also directional and acyclic. RELATED = an associative cross-link between concepts with no precedence — the integrative connective tissue, kept sparse [FACT for the enum values, source: APP_RECON entity schema; ESTIMATE for the learning-science mapping]. The critical discipline: keep prereq for genuine study-order dependencies only (it is the type that gates), keep part_of for composition, and do NOT let 'related' become a dumping ground — an over-used 'related' edge set is how a clean graph degrades into a hairball.

excluded: adding new edge types (out of scope; schema is fixed)
the color meaning layer that reads the types (its own node)

failure_modes: using prereq for merely-helpful relations and over-gating

nodes.definition: Fix what a Concept NODE should be: a single MASTERABLE, TESTABLE unit — a KST item — not a whole book chapter or a broad topic. The 'books -> fundamental units -> graph' vision means decomposing source material until each node is something a learner can be said to have mastered and a card can directly assess, which is the grain at which prerequisites, mastery estimates, and gating are meaningful [ESTIMATE — design synthesis over KST item semantics and concept-map concept-as-regularity]. Too COARSE (a node = 'Pharmacology') makes mastery and prerequisites meaningless; too FINE (a node per fact) explodes the graph and buries structure. The app's Concept is a per-exam named unit tied to cards [FACT-source: APP_RECON]; this node sets the authoring target grain: roughly one testable proposition-cluster per Concept, aligned to how cards tag concepts.

nodes.definition: Pin the boundary with contenteng and state what THIS KB's KST treatment adds. contenteng produces the edge table and explicitly DEFERS the full Knowledge Space Theory treatment [FACT-source: SPECIALIST_LIST §C1, KG_RECON §2a]. What KST adds on top of the raw edges: (1) knowledge STATES — a principled model of which combinations of mastered concepts are admissible, not just isolated mastery scores; (2) the learning FRINGE — a computed 'what to study next / what is unlocked' set; and (3) the surmise-based GATE — the prerequisite logic that turns edges into 'block until mastered'. KST-based adaptive assessment (efficiently locating a learner's state by choosing maximally informative items, the approach popularized by ALEKS) is the natural extension [ESTIMATE — to source-verify for the ALEKS attribution] but is beyond this app today; this KB claims the states/fringe/gate layer, not a full adaptive-assessment engine.

nodes.definition: Specify WHAT the color-coded data-and-meaning layer must express (leaving HOW to render it to the viz specialist). Each Concept node carries a MEANING to surface: its knowledge STATE membership (mastered / on the outer fringe / locked behind a prerequisite / not yet reachable) and its mastery level, and each edge carries its TYPE (prereq / part_of / related). The color layer's job is to make those two encodings legible at a glance — for example distinguishing a mastered concept from an unlocked-but-unstudied one from a still-locked one, and distinguishing a gating prereq edge from an associative related edge [ESTIMATE — design synthesis; the state categories derive from the KST nodes, the edge types from APP_RECON]. nodes.definition: Compose the recommended learning-science graph model, the go/no-go this KB builds toward. GO: a HIERARCHICAL concept-map backbone (part_of/hierarchy edges) as the spine; an acyclic PREREQUISITE DAG (prereq edges as surmise relations) driving the outer-fringe study frontier and the block-until-mastered gate with a hysteresis band; a SPARSE set of high-value 'related' cross-links for integration and retrieval; Concept nodes at masterable-unit grain; graduating FLAT-SPINE -> full graph only as evidence accrues; all mapped onto the existing Concept/ConceptEdge entities and feeding the color meaning layer and the prereq gate [ESTIMATE — design synthesis over the cited theory]. NO-GO: do NOT build a dense hairball, do NOT let 'related' become a catch-all, do NOT gate on a raw single-point threshold, and do NOT ship a prereq graph without an acyclicity check. An edge earns a place only when it expresses a real, evidence-justified learning relationship.

conflict_axes.name: qualitative_map_vs_formal_state_space
conflict_axes.description: Concept mapping models knowledge as human-readable labeled propositions while KST models it as a formal family of states, and the two do not reduce to each other.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: author the human-meaningful backbone as a concept-map hierarchy and let KST formalize its states and prerequisites for computation

conflict_axes.name: sparse_legible_vs_richly_connected
conflict_axes.description: A sparse hierarchical graph is legible and gives sequencing signal while a richly connected graph captures more relationships but trends toward an unusable hairball.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the graph a tree-plus-few-cross-links, add connectivity only when evidence justifies each edge

conflict_axes.name: anchor_hub_vs_bottleneck_hub
conflict_axes.description: A high-degree hub is a valuable integrative anchor but a prerequisite hub gates a large downstream subgraph and can become a bottleneck.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allow a few deliberate anchors but cap prereq out-degree and flag accidental high-degree hubs

conflict_axes.name: strict_gating_vs_learner_autonomy
conflict_axes.description: Strictly blocking new cards until prerequisites are mastered protects foundations but removes learner choice and can frustrate a ready learner.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate on a hysteresis band with an explicit deliberate escape hatch, not a hard immovable block

conflict_axes.name: hard_surmise_vs_soft_prerequisite
conflict_axes.description: The quasi-ordinal surmise relation treats prerequisites as hard implications, but real prerequisites are often merely helpful, so strict edges overstate necessity.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reserve prereq edges for genuine study-order necessity and route merely-helpful links to related

conflict_axes.name: point_threshold_vs_hysteresis_band
conflict_axes.description: Gating on a single mastery threshold is simple but flickers on estimate noise, while a hysteresis band is stable but adds a second parameter.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the app's 0.5/0.6 band as a hysteresis guard against threshold flicker

conflict_axes.name: coarse_vs_fine_node_granularity
conflict_axes.description: Coarse Concept nodes make mastery and prerequisites meaningless while overly fine nodes explode the graph and bury structure.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: target one masterable/testable unit per node, aligned to how cards tag concepts

conflict_axes.name: three_types_vs_relational_richness
conflict_axes.description: The fixed prereq/part_of/related enum keeps authoring consistent but cannot express every real relationship, tempting overload of 'related'.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep prereq strict, part_of for composition, and resist dumping every association into related; propose an enum extension only when a relation recurs

conflict_axes.name: build_full_graph_now_vs_graduate
conflict_axes.description: Building the full cross-linked graph up front captures integration immediately but risks a premature hairball, while graduating delays useful links.
poles: author the dense graph up front
graduate flat-spine to graph on evidence
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: start as a tree/spine and earn each cross-link with co-mastery or authoring evidence

workflow.gate: both failure directions and all four mitigations are stated, including the mandatory override

workflow.action: Map edge types and node granularity onto the app entities
workflow.description: Map prereq/part_of/related to relations and set the Concept node to a masterable unit
workflow.gate: each edge type is mapped to its relation (enum source-tagged) and the masterable-unit node grain is set

workflow.action: Define the color meaning contract and issue the graph-model verdict
workflow.description: Specify the node-state/edge-type meaning the colors must express and commit to the go/no-go graph model
workflow.gate: the color meaning contract and the go model (hierarchy backbone + acyclic prereq DAG + sparse cross-links + masterable nodes + staged graduation) plus the no-go list are stated on Concept/ConceptEdge

priority_rationale: The meaning-layer frame comes first because it decides which layer (meaning vs data vs render) every downstream decision belongs to; the concept-map features and the KST states/learning-space/fringe come next as the two theoretical poles that give nodes and edges their instructional meaning; the surmise relation and its acyclic prerequisite DAG then formalize the study-order structure; the graph-shape, hub, and retrieval nodes prescribe which shapes actually help; the gating mechanism, threshold band and gating risks operationalize block-until-mastered; and the edge-type semantics, node granularity, KST-vs-contenteng boundary, color meaning contract and final verdict come last because they compose every upstream idea into a concrete mapping onto the app's Concept/ConceptEdge entities with an explicit no-go on hairballs, catch-all edges, point-threshold gates and unchecked cycles.

dominance_rules.rule: Acyclicity of the prerequisite DAG dominates any convenience of adding an edge
dominance_rules.rationale: a cycle permanently locks concepts and breaks the learning-space accessibility guarantee
dominance_rules.trigger: a prereq edge is about to be added or a graph is about to gate
dominance_rules.action: run an acyclicity precheck and reject or break any cycle before using the graph

dominance_rules.rule: A masterable-unit node grain dominates chapter- or fact-level granularity
dominance_rules.rationale: prerequisites, mastery and gating are only meaningful when a node is a single testable unit
dominance_rules.action: decompose to one masterable/testable unit aligned to card concept-tags

dominance_rules.rule: Sparse hierarchy dominates dense connectivity when they conflict
dominance_rules.rationale: a hairball offers no sequencing signal and makes gates block almost everything
dominance_rules.trigger: connectivity is about to grow past a tree-plus-few-cross-links
dominance_rules.action: keep the graph sparse and add each cross-link only on evidence

dominance_rules.rule: A deliberate escape hatch dominates a hard immovable block
dominance_rules.rationale: a gate with no override lets one bad edge silently remove content
dominance_rules.action: always ship a deliberate learner/author override with the gate

dominance_rules.rule: The hysteresis band dominates a single-point unlock threshold
dominance_rules.rationale: a point threshold flickers on mastery-estimate noise
dominance_rules.trigger: the gate evaluates a borderline prerequisite mastery
dominance_rules.action: unlock at the higher bound and only re-lock below the lower bound (0.6/0.5)

dominance_rules.rule: Strict prereq typing dominates convenience use of prereq for helpful links
dominance_rules.rationale: prereq is the gating type, so a merely-helpful link marked prereq over-blocks
dominance_rules.trigger: a relationship is about to be typed prereq
dominance_rules.action: use prereq only for genuine surmise necessity and route helpful links to related

dominance_rules.rule: The KST states/fringe/gate layer dominates re-implementing contenteng's edge authoring
dominance_rules.rationale: contenteng owns edge authoring and defers KST; this KB adds the states/fringe/gate
dominance_rules.trigger: this KB's scope is about to overlap edge authoring
dominance_rules.action: claim only the KST states/fringe/gate layer and leave edge authoring to contenteng

dominance_rules.rule: The meaning contract dominates render choices in the color layer
dominance_rules.rationale: mixing palette/layout decisions into the meaning layer duplicates the viz specialist
dominance_rules.trigger: the color layer is being specified
dominance_rules.action: define only the node-state/edge-type distinctions the colors must express and defer palette/layout to viz

dominance_rules.rule: Text-only app rules are treated as unimplemented until code exists
dominance_rules.rationale: the block-until-mastered rule is diagnosis text with no enforcing code per APP_RECON
dominance_rules.trigger: an app behavior is cited as working
dominance_rules.action: verify enforcement against APP_RECON and specify the real gate before relying on the behavior

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the acyclicity precheck before any prerequisite gating is wired
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a shipped cyclic graph that permanently locks concepts and must be untangled after the gate is live

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the masterable-unit node grain before authoring nodes at scale
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-decomposing a whole deck when coarse or fine nodes make mastery and prerequisites meaningless

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the prereq/part_of/related type discipline before edges are authored
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a catch-all 'related' hairball that has to be re-typed edge by edge later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Start as a flat spine and graduate on evidence rather than building the dense graph up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: authoring a premature hairball whose unjustified edges must be pruned back

anti_rework_rules.rule: Specify the escape hatch when the gate is first designed, not after complaints
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retrofitting an override into a live gate that has been silently hiding content

anti_rework_rules.rule: Adopt the hysteresis band from the outset instead of a single threshold
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reworking a flickering point-threshold gate after learners see concepts toggle

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the block-until-mastered rule's enforcement against APP_RECON before building on it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building features atop a rule that is only diagnosis text and does not actually gate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Define the color meaning contract before viz picks a palette
anti_rework_rules.prevents: viz encoding the wrong or missing state categories and needing a re-color pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: an acyclicity check or a live gate reveals a cycle in the prereq DAG
iteration_protocol.action: break the cycle, re-run the check, and audit the affected concepts' unlockability
widen or confirm the hysteresis band and re-check the fringe computation

iteration_protocol.trigger: the 'related' edge set trends toward a hairball
iteration_protocol.action: re-audit related edges against the integrative-value bar and prune non-justified ones

iteration_protocol.trigger: an accidental prerequisite hub is found gating a large subgraph
iteration_protocol.action: review the hub's prereq out-degree and reroute or soften over-strict edges

iteration_protocol.trigger: co-mastery or authoring evidence justifies new integrative links
iteration_protocol.action: graduate the flat spine by adding the justified cross-links and re-checking acyclicity

iteration_protocol.trigger: an ESTIMATE-tagged learning-science claim (learning-space axioms, surmise/Birkhoff, ALEKS, Ausubel) is source-verified or refuted
iteration_protocol.action: update the affected node's tags and any recommendation resting on it

iteration_protocol.trigger: the viz layer reports a node-state or edge-type category it cannot render distinctly
iteration_protocol.action: revise the color meaning contract to make the required distinctions explicit

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
